text:
Andrei Kuzmenko is back in Los Angeles for the first time since leaving the Kings, where he played 74 games. He returns with a Penguins team that has gone four without a win (0-3-1), outscored 18-11, and that just took a 6-2 beating at home from Boston. The chances say the slide is only partly real (48% of the expected goals): Pittsburgh won the chance battle in three of its last five games and has one win to show for it.

The rest is noise you can't ignore. Headlines this week have Pittsburgh "Fielding Calls On Rickard Rakell" (NHL Trade Rumors) and Evgeni Malkin preparing a trade list (NHL Trade Talk). Bryan Rust is out with a lower-body injury until around Dec 5, so Tommy Novak has moved up beside Sidney Crosby and Rakell at 18:10 a night. Arturs Silovs has stopped .876 this season after finishing last year 12.8 goals worse than expected, and the power play creates only 0.46 expected goals a game.

The Kings have been rolling more than their 3-2-0 record suggests, with more of the expected goals in four of their last five. Their last game was a 7-2 win over the Sharks: Adrian Kempe had a hat trick and passed Dustin Brown on the franchise list, and Artemi Panarin added four assists. Alex Laferriere is the one Kings forward still waiting: no goals in eight games on 4.3 expected goals. Our sleeper is Quinton Byfield, 53% for a point with his ice time projected at 20:23. Trevor Moore plays his 500th game and Joel Edmundson his 700th.

Both teams sit at 12 points. Our numbers have it 3.20 to 3.02 for Los Angeles, and the Kings take 4.2 penalties a game, which gives even this Pittsburgh power play a few looks.
headline: Kuzmenko returns to a Kings team in form

hunch.text: Laferriere's drought ends: eight games and 4.3 expected goals without a goal is a run of bad bounces, and the Penguins' goaltending has been giving out good ones.
